title: Architecture: In-App Messaging & Trade Chat — xCube
overview: The messaging feature adds a real-time channel-based chat layer to xCube. The architecture prioritises sub-500ms delivery latency, horizontal scalability to 10,000 concurrent connections, and a compliant 7-year message retention pipeline. The new Message Service sits alongside existing xCube backend services, reusing PostgreSQL (RDS) for channel metadata and adding Cassandra for message storage and Redis Pub/Sub for fan-out.

backend.rationale: Write throughput at scale without contention; native TTL support for 7-year retention; channel-partitioned queries are trivially fast via partition key design

backend.alternatives: Kafka, RabbitMQ, WebSocket broadcast per pod
backend.rationale: Already in stack; sub-millisecond fan-out; stateless Message Service pods all subscribe to the same Pub/Sub topic per channel
Blocklist, URL detection, and velocity checks (same ticker >10× in 5 min) are deterministic and synchronous — zero latency cost
Pump-and-dump detection and nuanced investment advice flagging require semantic understanding; target >92% precision; async to avoid delivery latency impact

backend.alternatives: Periodic batch export, direct S3 write from Message Service
backend.rationale: Change-data capture ensures no messages are missed even on crash; Parquet on S3 enables cost-effective Athena queries for compliance team

infrastructure.alternatives: AWS API Gateway WebSocket, custom Node.js proxy
infrastructure.rationale: TLS termination, connection upgrade, sticky-sessions not required (Redis-backed fan-out handles cross-instance delivery)
Existing cluster; stateless pods scale horizontally; 5 pods × 2,000 connections = 10,000 target

entities.name: channels (PostgreSQL)
entities.key_fields: name TEXT UNIQUE, topic TEXT, created_by UUID, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ, member_count INT
entities.notes: PostgreSQL chosen for channel metadata — relational, low write volume, ACID guarantees needed for member_count updates

entities.name: channel_members (PostgreSQL)
entities.relationships: N:1 with channels, N:1 with users
entities.notes: Simple membership join table; index on user_id for 'my channels' query

entities.name: messages (Cassandra)
entities.primary_key: channel_id UUID PARTITION KEY, created_at TIMESTAMP CLUSTERING KEY DESC
entities.key_fields: message_id UUID, user_id UUID, content TEXT, ticker_ref TEXT (JSON nullable), moderation_status TEXT (approved|pending|rejected)
entities.notes: Partition by channel_id; clustering DESC gives most-recent-first reads without sorting; TTL = 7 years per row

entities.name: Redis keys
entities.key_fields: channel:{id}:subscribers SET, ratelimit:msg:{user_id} sliding window counter (max 30/min), Pub/Sub topic ch:{channel_id}
entities.notes: All Redis state is ephemeral; reconnect recovers from Cassandra history

data_model.entity_relationship_diagram:
users 1──N channel_members N──1 channels
channels 1──N messages (Cassandra)

endpoints.purpose: List public channels paginated by activity

endpoints.notes: Reads from Cassandra; cursor is created_at of oldest returned message

endpoints.response: JSON frames per message or ticker update
endpoints.notes: Client sends subscribe/send/unsubscribe frames; server pushes message and ticker_update frames; moderation_held frame if message is flagged

repository_impact.changes_required: New channels and messages services; Cassandra client + schema migrations; Redis Pub/Sub fan-out; Moderation Service (rule-based + LLM classifier); WebSocket gateway integration; Archive pipeline (Debezium + Kafka producer)
repository_impact.notes: Message Service pods are stateless — scale independently from existing API pods

repository_impact.changes_required: New Chat tab in bottom nav; channel browser, channel detail with message thread; compose box with ticker card attachment; WebSocket manager for real-time messages; deep-link handler for ticker card tap
repository_impact.notes: Ticker card price updates via existing quote WebSocket; no new quote infrastructure on mobile

repository_impact.changes_required: New Chat tab; channel list fragment; message thread RecyclerView with DiffUtil; ticker card ViewHolder; WebSocket connection manager; deep-link handler
repository_impact.notes: Background message delivery via FCM for unread notifications (Phase 2); MVP is foreground-only

system_diagram:
Mobile Client (iOS / Android)
   ├── REST HTTPS → API Gateway → Channels Service (Node.js) → PostgreSQL RDS
   └── WebSocket WSS → WS Gateway (Nginx) → Message Service (Node.js)
                                                    ├── Redis Pub/Sub (fan-out to other pods)
                                                    ├── Cassandra (message store)
                                                    └── Moderation Service
                                                            ├── Rule-based classifier (<5ms)
                                                            └── LLM Classifier (~200ms async)
                                                                    └── Human Review Queue (Slack)
Archive Pipeline:
   Cassandra → Debezium CDC → Kafka (messages.archive) → S3 (Parquet) → Athena (compliance)

data_flows.name: Message send and delivery
steps: Client sends WebSocket frame: {type: 'send', channelId, content, tickerRef}
Message Service receives frame; runs rule-based moderation (<5ms)
If rule-based passes: write to Cassandra with moderation_status=approved
Publish message to Redis Pub/Sub topic ch:{channelId}
All Message Service pods subscribed to that topic push message frame to their connected clients
Async: LLM classifier evaluates for pump-and-dump signals; if flagged, status updated to pending and human review queue notified
Human reviewer approves or rejects; if approved, message retroactively delivered to clients who missed it

data_flows.name: Ticker card real-time update
steps: Client receives a message frame containing tickerCard with symbol
Message Service subscribes to Market Data WebSocket quote stream for that symbol
Every 15 seconds, Market Data emits a price update for the symbol
Message Service pushes ticker_update frame to all clients in the channel who have that ticker card visible

infrastructure.hosting: Message Service on existing AWS ECS Fargate cluster: 5 tasks × 1 vCPU / 2GB RAM; auto-scales to 20 at peak. Cassandra: 3-node EC2 cluster (r6g.xlarge) in us-east-1. Kafka: MSK (2 brokers). WS Gateway: 2 Nginx tasks on Fargate.
infrastructure.cost_estimate: Cassandra EC2 (3× r6g.xlarge): ~$300/mo. Kafka MSK (2 brokers): ~$120/mo. S3 archive (7 years at 10GB/mo growth): ~$25/mo first year. ECS Message Service incremental: ~$60/mo. Total incremental: ~$505/mo for 10K users ($0.05/user/month).
deployment_pipeline: Cassandra schema changes via schema migration tool (Cassandra Migrations) on deploy
ECS Fargate blue/green deployment via CodeDeploy for Message Service
Kafka topic creation via Terraform; MSK cluster changes gated behind manual approval in CI
LLM classifier prompt version-controlled in repo; updated without service restart

failure_modes.mitigation: Message Service falls back to direct Cassandra write + read; fan-out disabled (messages persist but not real-time); PagerDuty alert
3-node cluster with RF=3; loss of 1 node is transparent; loss of 2 nodes triggers read-only mode; PagerDuty P1
Rule-based classifier remains active; LLM stage skipped; messages delivered after rule-based pass; human review queue batched for catchup when LLM recovers
Clients reconnect to any available pod within 5s (exponential backoff); Redis Pub/Sub subscription rebuilt on reconnect; message history loaded from Cassandra

security_considerations: All WebSocket connections authenticated via JWT query parameter; connection rejected immediately if token invalid or expired
Rate limiting: 30 messages/minute per user enforced via Redis sliding window; violators receive 429 WebSocket error frame
All message content encrypted at rest in Cassandra (AES-256); S3 archive uses SSE-S3
Channel moderation audit log retained alongside messages for compliance; human review decisions immutable
Influencer channel partnerships subject to legal review — disclosure requirements if influencer holds positions discussed in their channel
Message content must never be returned in error responses or server logs — only message IDs and metadata

new_dependencies.name: Apache Cassandra
new_dependencies.not_solvable_with_existing_stack_because: PostgreSQL cannot sustain the projected 50K writes/sec at market open without severe contention on message rows; Cassandra's partition-key model aligns naturally with channel-scoped queries and provides native TTL for 7-year retention at scale.
new_dependencies.existing_alternatives_evaluated: PostgreSQL (existing) — ruled out due to write throughput ceiling at scale. DynamoDB — considered but cross-region complexity and vendor lock-in outweighed benefits. MongoDB — already ruled out in team decision log.
new_dependencies.cost_or_risk: Operational overhead of managing a 3-node Cassandra cluster; requires dedicated DBA runbook and oncall rotation. License: Apache 2.0 (free). Estimated infra cost: ~$350/mo for r6g.xlarge × 3.

new_dependencies.name: Debezium CDC + Kafka
new_dependencies.not_solvable_with_existing_stack_because: The compliance archive requirement demands zero-loss capture of every message written to Cassandra, including crash scenarios. Periodic batch export from the Message Service cannot guarantee completeness. Debezium CDC tails the Cassandra commit log; Kafka provides durable buffering before S3.
new_dependencies.existing_alternatives_evaluated: Direct S3 write from Message Service — ruled out because a pod crash between write and S3 push would silently lose messages. Redis Streams — cannot replay Cassandra's commit log; insufficient durability for compliance purposes.
new_dependencies.cost_or_risk: Adds Kafka cluster (3 brokers) ~$180/mo on MSK. Debezium connector requires JVM process alongside each Cassandra node. Team must be trained on Debezium offset management.

open_questions.decision: Cassandra cluster sizing for 3-year message volume at 10K MAU sending 10 messages/day
open_questions.recommendation: Model at 10B messages/year; r6g.xlarge × 3 handles ~50K writes/sec — sufficient. Review at 50K MAU milestone.
open_questions.risk: Under-provisioned cluster causes write failures at market open peak

open_questions.decision: LLM classifier model selection for moderation
open_questions.recommendation: Claude Haiku for cost-efficiency (~$0.0003/message); evaluate Mistral as fallback; do not use GPT-4 at MVP volumes due to cost
open_questions.risk: Model prompt injection via crafted message content — test adversarially before launch

open_questions.decision: Message hold vs. deliver-then-remove for flagged content
open_questions.recommendation: Hold before delivery for MVP (safer); accept latency cost for flagged messages; revisit if false-positive rate >5% creates UX complaints
open_questions.risk: Hold approach means legitimate messages may be delayed 10–30 minutes during human review queue backup

features.title: Channel Infrastructure & Real-Time Messaging
features.cross_repo_boundaries: iOS/Android call REST /api/channels for CRUD and history; connect WebSocket /ws/chat for real-time; Message Service fans out via Redis Pub/Sub across stateless pods
features.technical_notes: WebSocket pods are stateless — each subscribes to Redis Pub/Sub topics for channels their connected clients have joined. Rate limit enforced at Message Service ingestion, not gateway, to avoid Redis round-trip on gateway.
risks: Cassandra partition hotspot if a single channel (e.g. #aapl-watchers at earnings) receives >10K msg/min — add sub-partitioning by hour if needed
Redis Pub/Sub fan-out at 10K concurrent connections with 5 pods = 2K subs per pod × topic delivery — benchmark at load

features.title: Ticker Card Sharing & Order Flow Integration
features.cross_repo_boundaries: Message Service subscribes to existing Market Data WebSocket for ticker symbols referenced in active cards; pushes ticker_update frames to chat clients every 15s; deep-link handled natively on iOS/Android
features.technical_notes: Ticker card price updates are pushed by Message Service, not polled by clients, to avoid N×M polling (N clients × M tickers). Message Service maintains a set of active ticker subscriptions per Cassandra-connected channel. Deep-link must pre-fill order direction (buy/sell) — derive from message context or default to buy.
risks: Message Service must unsubscribe from ticker quote stream when no clients are viewing the card — otherwise subscription leaks accumulate over time

features.title: Content Moderation & Compliance Archive
features.cross_repo_boundaries: Moderation Service is a module within xcube-api (not a separate service at MVP); Debezium CDC connector reads Cassandra and produces to Kafka from xcube-data-infra; S3/Athena managed in data-infra repo
features.technical_notes: Rule-based moderation is synchronous (<5ms) and runs inline before Cassandra write. LLM classifier runs async after write — message is delivered on rule-based pass, then retroactively held and removed from client cache if LLM flags it. Slack webhook for human review is MVP-only; replace with internal review UI in Phase 2.
risks: Debezium CDC on Cassandra requires kafka-connect-cassandra plugin — validate compatibility with MSK Connect before provisioning
LLM classifier prompt injection via crafted message — add input sanitisation and test adversarially in staging
